title: 4.1.6 import memory control: ownership, progress, byte batching and spill
authorization: User requests all remaining memory-control fixes and CSV alignment; online resizing and non-glibc platforms excluded.

design_gate.trigger: Crosses allocation, operator, spill-file and compiler ownership; adds cancellable admission coordination and shared spill-source lifecycle. Design-first required by mo-dev.

problem_evidence: Stock first complete import succeeds and second fails under 22 GiB; idle writer capacity and allocator resident free pages contribute to history dependence.

V2 closes one cleanup leak, bounds idle Arena bytes and adds native trim; five uninterrupted 39-table rounds pass, but review identifies impossible-admission, reclaim-threshold-gap, retained-delete reservation and incomplete upstream bounds.
Per-writer 20 ms ForceRefresh causes redundant process sampling/reclaim and has no fairness guarantee.
CSV currently limits raw input field bytes; MultiUpdate projections and vector capacities can amplify the next allocation.
HashBuild spills only shuffle, copies before testing the threshold; scatter buffers are row bounded and max-depth skew reload is unbounded.

Deterministic compiler fixtures: after full reclaim permits 64 MiB, old solver grants 4 bytes; max-row floor with identical envelopes shrinks 64 to 32 MiB despite no memory benefit. This is a throughput defect, not yet an explanation of the interrupted native table 29.

Final candidate581d746 failed faithful table21 am_case_comprehensive_dataset after20 successes: old insert.Insert returned exhausted on three tries (ask720360..765440, Available about21GB), while RSS peak3.804GiB and cgroup OOM events0. Independent isolated original-schema/original-CSV reproduction also fails. Compiler already reserved old Insert output I/W but the consumer never used them.

Frozen v8 f082 binary: fresh independent two-process CN remote controlled broadcast INSERT JOIN fails with1105 broadcast spill generation is unavailable. An old-source overlay adding actual Free immediately after the existing first.Reset deterministically reproduces the same named failure (reset-free-repro.json, exit1 after successful compilation). Pipeline cleanup retires an early nonfinalizer while another expected actual is still collecting; successful registration was reset to false, so Free incorrectly aborts the shared generation.

Independent review of 0c69895511 reproduced seven failures: partition metadata frame loss, shared-varlen copy expansion, undersized clone promises, retry label mutation, unbounded fused projections admitted as bounded, deferred delete credit refunded before materialization, and unconditional legacy expression-key spill. Sibling audits confirmed partition-writer terminal cleanup and partial-allocation cleanup defects.

Actual TKE cgroup v1 private bind has mount root equal to process membership. Old dependency repeats the membership under the exposed mountpoint, misses valid accounting files, and leaves a 1.87GiB LOAD waiting despite actual usage419MiB/limit55GiB. Two full-CN dumps, actual process/mount/stat files and node-RAM equality close the cause; local v2 acceptance did not cover this runtime layout.
goals: The tested amway import semantics, indexes, row counts and SQL success remain intact under fixed 22 GiB and no inter-round idle/GC/restart.
Every satisfiable admission wait is driven by owner release or reclaim, not an independent 20 ms polling loop.
Every large import-owned buffer retains a budget charge until destruction or a documented transfer.
Normal writer reuse and asynchronous IO are preserved where budgets permit.
Input and spill frames are bounded by actual typed bytes, not only rows or raw CSV bytes.
Broadcast and skew spill produce complete join semantics without unbounded reload.
exclusions: Adding native trim support for non-glibc systems
Remote publication or release without existing authorization
Guaranteeing success when a single irreducible row or minimum query working set cannot fit the environment, or external allocations consume the entire shared cgroup

Providing a finite working-set guarantee for arbitrary variable-length SQL function expansion without a pre-evaluation capacity contract; these statements retain legacy execution, including the existing unrestricted skew fallback where applicable.

invariants.Q1: Each reservation, workspace, owned buffer and spill FD has exactly one effective terminal owner; transfer keeps the charge/source alive until the consumer releases it.
invariants.Q2: A task cannot wait for normal data credits while holding the only workspace that is needed to free those data credits. Reclaim and cancellation never depend on the blocked writer.
invariants.Q3: Input batch, private retained capacity, pending jobs, spill bucket buffers, spill frames and skew working sets have byte bounds. A cache limit alone is not an active-memory limit.
invariants.accounting: Use per-owner allocated capacity, not cumulative processed input. Go and native pool allocations both count; serialization/map/bitmap state has an explicit capacity charge.
invariants.progress: Too-large requests are split before waiting. Physical-pressure denial drives one merged reclaim+fresh sample even below the RSS soft line. Pool denial waits for actual ownership release.
invariants.performance: No per-writer periodic sampling; hot-path accounting reuses atomic counters and row-window boundaries, with no full retained-state scan for every row.
invariants.largest_fitting_unit: At admission linearization select the largest legal unit fitting the current physical and shared I/W state. Reclaim/release must reconsider larger candidates. Identical complete envelopes preserve the largest unit; reducing an execution unit without reducing its promise is not progress.

decisions.choice: Retain nonblocking RSCThrottler compatibility; add optional cancellable admission, request-size and byte-unit capabilities.
decisions.rationale: Existing mocks and nonblocking spill decisions remain compatible.

decisions.choice: FIFO notification-driven waits with a single process coordinator and a one-second fallback only while waiters exist.
decisions.rationale: Release/reclaim events wake immediately; fallback observes external frees without 50*N process samples per second. A queued request cannot be bypassed by new ordinary grants.

decisions.choice: Native/process reclamation is single flight and cancellation-independent; denied physical admission may request reclaim below 85% RSS.
decisions.rationale: Closes the confirmed 17+6>22 GiB threshold gap without lowering a magic percentage.

decisions.choice: Calibrate physical pressure using process RSS and same-cgroup usage after separating reclaimable inactive file cache; do not add RSS and cgroup usage.
decisions.rationale: The signals overlap and must not be double counted. Keep raw cgroup usage observable.

decisions.choice: Released grants lose their old RSS-covered credit; reclaimable libc pages count as resident until a fresh sample proves they returned.
decisions.rationale: Cross-arena free chunks are not guaranteed headroom for a new owner.

decisions.choice: Use one byte-unit policy for CSV, writer subbatches and spill frames. CSV enforces raw and typed capacity bounds; MultiUpdate rechecks all actual projections.
decisions.rationale: CSV cannot infer every downstream index projection. Varlen windows must count referenced payload rather than their shared entire area.

decisions.choice: MultiUpdate uses a private accounting mpool and an owned-capacity counter that includes Go and native buffers; all retained delete/index metadata remain charged.
decisions.rationale: A shared process mpool delta cannot identify this writer's ownership, especially with async jobs.

decisions.choice: Separate ordinary retained data grants from a bounded process IO/spill workspace permit. A spill/IO worker never waits for ordinary data grants held by its submitter.
decisions.rationale: Prevents the main-Sync to worker-budget wait cycle. Workspace is acquired before writing and transferred with jobs, then released on success/error/cancel.

decisions.choice: Before mutation reserve a conservative computed append/serialization growth envelope; after the operation reconcile to actual retained capacity.
decisions.rationale: Accounting only after allocation cannot bound a temporary resize/clone peak. Envelope derives from vector growth and encoded/compression sizes, not customer data names.

decisions.choice: Keep total idle Arena byte cap, but share its budget across size tiers on demand.
decisions.rationale: A tier cannot discard useful buffers while the other tier leaves budget unused. Checked-out ownership remains separate from idle cache.

decisions.choice: HashBuild requests retained-data budget before copying; denial starts spill using the reserved IO workspace.
decisions.rationale: No build operator holds its data waiting for a downstream writer to free memory.

decisions.choice: Broadcast spill retains a shared immutable build source. Probe streams spool bounded files; after all participants register, a single spill consumer owns combined probe sources and executes the existing join semantics.
decisions.rationale: Preserves right/full/semi/anti/single matching without incompatible per-probe bitmaps or an on-the-fly shuffle protocol. Only the spill path serializes; normal broadcast parallelism stays unchanged.

decisions.choice: Skew fallback at the recursion bound uses bounded build chunks and replays probe data, with disk sidecar match state where needed.
decisions.rationale: All-equal keys cannot be fixed by more repartitioning. Preserve LEFT/FULL/SEMI/ANTI/SINGLE cross-chunk match semantics without loading the entire bucket.

decisions.choice: Serialize spill frames without a second unbounded whole-batch copy; limit scatter by aggregate bytes across buckets before Union.
decisions.rationale: Spilling must not reproduce the original wide-row memory peak.

decisions.choice: Enable statement working sets only for whole-DAG bounded CSV sources and join-key expression contracts supported before evaluation. Column keys, fixed-width expressions and bounded serial/composite keys share one capacity derivation for normal hash, spill and skew. Unknown variable-length expression expansion retains whole-query legacy execution.
decisions.rationale: The CSV raw-record limit does not bound generic table scans or arbitrary expression expansion. Fallback must preserve legal query semantics and cannot advertise unbounded operators as admitted memory.

decisions.choice: Control streams use a separate backend pool and caller context during backend acquisition. Returned stream lifetime remains explicit and independent. Board cleanup occurs only after closed root plus final attached scope cleanup.
decisions.rationale: A control owner must not consume the last execution connection, and cancelling a scope does not prove it has stopped reading shared buffers.

decisions.choice: Probe process-instance UUID with admission capability. If a statement includes multiple CNs sharing one process coordinator, use whole-query legacy. Otherwise acquire in (process UUID,CN UUID) order and validate expected process UUID before every Open/Reserve.
decisions.rationale: CN ordering is insufficient when distinct CN identities alias one process coordinator: one statement can self-wait, and two statements can introduce opposite physical-process edges through different CN aliases. An Open epoch check prevents a restart after capability discovery from changing the ordering identity.

decisions.choice: Use the early irregular-index source only for FAIL/ordinary LOAD. IGNORE maintenance consumes a final projection downstream of duplicate filtering, with or without regular indexes. UPDATE also consumes final images and alone emits old-index deletes.
decisions.rationale: Public SQL showed ignored duplicate-PK text leaking into FT while the base row and BTREE remained correct after the UPDATE-only guard. The original mixed-index code accidentally restored the filtered source; retain correct IGNORE filtering without recreating the unnecessary ordinary-LOAD old-table join.

decisions.choice: Compiler prepares at most 27 descending power-of-two legal working-set candidates. Optional ReserveWorkingSetCandidates uses one existing FIFO node and selects the largest physically fitting candidate atomically under the coordinator mutex after every relevant wake. Single-spec Reserve delegates to the same implementation.
decisions.rationale: Resetting the unit only after synchronous reclaim leaves stale small units in FIFO waiters; waiting only for the largest target can reject progress when a smaller unit would fit. A bounded candidate list avoids either failure without a new worker, polling loop, user parameter or per-row work.
constraints: Deduplicate only identical full I/W envelopes (including input layout), never equal totals with different input/workspace decomposition. Fit uses input+max(0,IO-currentWorkspacePromise).
Preserve FIFO ordering and context removal/rollback; no second node or partial promise. Candidate specs are immutable/owned for the duration of a wait.

FIFO head with no active owners performs one existing merged full reclaim outside the mutex. It rescans all candidates under the mutex; if none fit, it removes its node and returns a typed minimum-capacity error enabling compiler DOP retry. The same transition applies after the last owner exits while waiting.

Known sample invalidity does not create credit; existing cancellation, one-second shared fallback and mixed-version legacy behavior remain unchanged. DOP recompilation releases partial statement tickets.
alternatives_rejected: Reset unit to target only after Reclaim: leaves owner-release/FIFO case stale.
Queue only the maximum target: can block forever even when smaller valid layout fits the fixed resident baseline.

decisions.choice: Connect disk ToWriteS3 old Insert to the existing statement output/input and single-IO working set, using existing CNS3Writer/Sinker/stream codec. Preserve old no-working-set write behavior. Replace old flush-limiter polling with release/context notifications.
decisions.rationale: Merely waiting or suppressing an error cannot make D fit while this same statement holds its declared I/W promises; old writer metadata also accumulated until Eval. Existing multi_update already supplies the applicable ownership pattern, and the old Insert output protocol can remain unchanged.
alternatives_rejected: Convert all old Inserts to MultiUpdate: changes planner and MergeBlock protocol beyond the missing consumer boundary.
Only retry D or increase physical thresholds: can self-wait or restore unbounded allocation.
Always write every small input directly: discards normal buffered reuse and async IO even when retained-data memory is available.

decisions.choice: Separate a sealed topology handle from execution-participant ownership. Track one local participant state none/expected/registered/finalizer/retired, and route Reset/Free through one idempotent retirement transition.
decisions.classification: Focused correction within the already approved CN-local broadcast owner model; record and narrowly review its concrete lifecycle deviation before implementation. No new wire format, resource bound, scheduler or fallback.
decisions.rationale: A Boolean registered flag cannot distinguish an unexecuted compiler template, an actual that failed before registration, and an actual that successfully handed its probe files to the group. Real Pipeline.Cleanup Reset-to-Free ordering must be safe while other actuals remain active.
constraints: Sealing the expected topology alone acquires no execution owner. Freeing or resetting an unexecuted template must not abort any actual or a later epoch.

Every actual must acquire the expected state before execution or initialization can fail, including duplicated actuals and the Mcpu=1 original. Prepare arms idempotently before any lease/expression initialization; concrete compiler construction/early-failure hooks must be reviewed.
Register success transfers probe files into the existing group and advances state to registered. Normal nonfinalizer retirement does not abort or close those transferred files.

Claiming finalizer advances state; exhausted normal work closes via the existing sole work owner. Early termination/error/cancel aborts collection and then closes work, never concurrently closing a reader-owned FD.
Retirement is once per actual generation; repeated Reset/Free cannot decrement or abort again. A subsequent Prepare/new generation explicitly rearms; a stale handle cannot abort the new epoch.

Normal in-memory participant completion calls FinishParticipant once. Keep the nonowning generation handle for the existing spill-aware bitmap guard; do not accidentally resume the old bitmap protocol after local retirement.
No controller bypass, threshold inflation, spill disablement or weaker multi-CN oracle.
Normal non-spilled/empty-build completion calls FinishParticipant exactly once, not Abort. Pipeline.Cleanup cancels contexts on normal exit too; proc.Ctx.Err alone is not a success/failure oracle.

Inspect the actual compiler hooks and test the real consumer sequence. Arm expected actual ownership before scheduler/reader/Prepare failures; never infer ownership merely from a sealed template topology.

decisions.choice: Correct copy bounds at vector ownership and preserve shared varlen areas when no larger than referenced payload; use the same copy sizing for full and partial hash-build batches, including bitmap capacity and allocation failure cleanup. Ordinary legacy joins only spill on real pressure.
decisions.rationale: A prediction must describe the allocation actually performed; unsupported static bounds are not memory pressure for a legacy query.

decisions.choice: PartitionMultiUpdate drains exactly one producer frame per Call and destroys every active/retired writer on terminal cleanup. Deferred committed-delete materialization remains charged until corresponding prepared state is destroyed or transferred, and its worst-case footprint sets the delete window.
decisions.rationale: The producer now streams metadata. A double Call drops frames; reconciling only present buffers discards future credits before the corresponding bitmap/map/vector is allocated.

decisions.choice: NewCompile owns a clone of caller routing labels. Every DOP retry and pool cleanup preserves the original selector.
decisions.rationale: A rebuilt Compile can be released before the next retry without deleting routing labels in the original Compile.

decisions.choice: Memory admission version 2 includes immutable, validated producer descriptors and dedicated expression/embedded-producer I promises per actual executor. Bounds propagate source rows and per-column payload through projections, filters, shuffles, merges, joins and the audited default tokenizer Apply. Every receiver derives the full promise without executing SQL.
decisions.rationale: Raw CSV input bytes do not bound fused expression outputs, scratch, or hidden table-function producers. A whole-DAG claim must cover those allocations explicitly.
constraints: Descriptor dependencies are topological and validated, with checked arithmetic, real executor counts and real result-column lineage. Schema widths are finite only when the physical path enforces that bound.
CSV bounds include its legal crossing row; generic unbounded scans, opaque producers and unsupported expressions choose whole-query legacy before any Open.
Shared key-expression contract derives output and all simultaneously live intermediate buffers. Promises remain live through real nonprepared operator Free.
Prepared queries retain executor capacity across Reset; until there is a separate retained-owner contract they select whole-query legacy before admission, including subsequent executions.

Default/ngram fulltext_index_tokenize gets a table_function-owned bound covering content copies, tokenizer scratch, Document.Words growth/copies, bounded output, argument expressions and actual Apply result columns. Datalink and unproven parsers choose whole-query legacy.

All remote peers must advertise protocol version 2 before Open; old bool-only or vanilla peers select legacy. Unknown manifest versions/roles are rejected before execution. No new tuning parameter, polling worker, customer name or fixed incident shape.

Controlled default tokenizer and CROSS Apply output are byte chunked using the same unit with a legal singleton exception. Actual document arguments and Apply result columns determine runtime chunk rows; no data is skipped, replayed or truncated. OUTER or unaudited TVF modes select legacy.

decisions.choice: Prove and charge local transfer queues and retained operator copies explicitly. Controlled pSpool idle caches retain at most the shared unit per cache ID; only the final receiver return can free an oversized idle cache. Its active clones and replacement peaks have dedicated producer I promises. PreInsert copies and supported LockOp key/packer/nullable/refresh buffers receive explicit promises at the same root.
decisions.rationale: A byte-bounded CSV does not bound multiple queued deep copies or independently retained operator capacity. Deriving a per-column lifetime high-water from unrelated maximum-sized rows also produces an unusable promise; bounded idle reuse closes that state without a user knob.
constraints: Keep active borrowed frames valid through final reader release; apply the cap at quiescent cache return only, with no active truncation.
Keep the existing legacy spool policy when there is no statement working set. Destroy all controlled caches before the root promise is released.
Unknown retaining operators (including unbounded shuffle buckets, FuzzyFilter cardinality/collision state and deferred PostDml SQL lists) select whole-query legacy before Open.

Remote CSV edges currently include uncharged backend codecs, queues and reassembly pools with independent lifetimes. Until that ownership is explicitly bounded, those complete statements select legacy before opening any admission controls; ordinary local CSV imports stay controlled.
This safe support-domain correction does not reject a legal query or claim an OOM guarantee for a legacy path. Non-CSV queries retain their existing path.
LockOp Packer uses class-backed Go storage; its bound follows ClassAllocationSize rather than assuming libc malloc.

Local Dispatch fanout metadata includes C separately rounded receiver queues, each with nextPowerOfTwo(max(2,C)) message slots, plus receiver/slot/ref/cache headers. Derive checked capacity from the first owner; the quadratic C-squared term cannot be replaced with a linear clone allowance or an arbitrary fanout cap.

decisions.choice: Every local spool has a final query-attempt owner in BaseProcess. Register immediately after creation, before later Prepare steps can fail. After all local pipeline/notify/IO owners have joined, the joined attempt/RPC boundary drains the BaseProcess registries and calls CloseAfterReadersStopped before restoring views, detaching or closing the working-set root.
decisions.rationale: Normal ForceCleanup must preserve queued/borrowed frames until End. Cleanup timeouts can leave End undelivered; dropping the operator pointer and destroying an MPool does not free those native buffers. A query root knows when there can no longer be a reader, so it is the correct final destructor. Data signal sends must observe query cancellation so a missing receiver cannot block the join required by final destruction.
constraints: Register every local spool, including legacy. Only the joined attempt/RPC boundary collects legacy registries, checking each BaseProcess has no unowned ImportMemory; never collect them from an inactive Compile.clear or Process.Free. Controlled roots also collect installed views before memory-detach/Close.

Track occupied message slots; last receiver return clears the slot before returning its id. The final destructor frees only still-occupied owned clones plus remaining idle storage, and shares the existing cleanupOnce.
Final destruction does not wait for End or mutate drainedReceivers; caller must already have joined all senders and readers. Normal ForceCleanup continues to preserve outstanding borrowers.
Copy failure returns both the cache ID and the message slot; partial initialization stays atomic.
Registries are mutex protected, taken and cleared per attempt, and do not survive a completed attempt into reuse.

design_review.evidence: Verified runOnce root errC closure, Scope.Run deferred Pipeline.Cleanup, Scope.MergeRun deferred wg.Wait including notify cleanup, and fresh BaseProcess in remote decode. Independent reviewer also approved legacy extension with per-Base unowned-ticket guards and cleanup only at the real joined attempt/RPC boundary.

decisions.superseded_contract: The historical mechanism below is retained only as problem/review evidence. Revision20 D36 is normative: official durable typed terminal, DiscardUnsent, independent cache/final once, preallocated Abort scratch, joined edge drain -> final slot cleanup -> registry removal -> root ticket release. No occupied/publicationFailed or legacy spool End/ack on typed paths.

decisions.choice: Treat a local spool data enqueue and its external Ch2 publication as one ownership protocol. Record a publication failure on that exact spool generation. After any data publication fails, terminal cleanup sends direct End markers to every local receiver, does not enqueue a spool End, and does not wait for spool acknowledgements. Preserve every previously published borrower and transfer abandoned frames to the existing joined-attempt destructor.
decisions.rationale: Native LIMIT1 on 2bacd2829a returned after30s with three missing End markers. Cancellation between spool enqueue and Ch2 notification orphaned a data entry. The later token intended for a spool End popped that data instead, so receiver nil counts never reached zero. Call-only cancellation tests skipped the real Reset/drain protocol.
constraints: Normal successful publication retains the existing ordered spool End/ack protocol. No timeout reduction, unconditional receiver bypass or premature destruction.
The publication state belongs to the spool generation and is set by a shared data-publication helper; cover Connector plus all/any/index/local-match/multi-match Dispatch routes.

A direct terminal token follows all successfully published tokens on each receiver channel. Active broadcast borrowers stay valid until release; unpublished references remain owned until every pipeline joins.
Only the joined attempt/RPC boundary may finally destroy unacknowledged frames. Operator Reset may retain cleanupSpool and attempt ordinary ForceCleanup, which must preserve borrowers.

Deterministic regressions execute canceled publication -> actual Reset -> real receiver drain -> joined final destruction. Their End markers must come only from Reset, and broadcast tests must include one successful reader plus one failed publication.

design_review.evidence: F/pipeline-publication-review.json establishes enqueue-before-publish -> orphaned queue head -> spool-End token consumes data -> missing receiver End. Reviewer proposed generation-local broken-publication mode, direct terminal markers, preserved live broadcast borrowers and joined ownership. Root approved that design before code changes.

decisions.superseded_contract: The historical mechanism below is retained only as problem/review evidence. Revision20 D36 is normative: official durable typed terminal, DiscardUnsent, independent cache/final once, preallocated Abort scratch, joined edge drain -> final slot cleanup -> registry removal -> root ticket release. No occupied/publicationFailed or legacy spool End/ack on typed paths.

decisions.choice: Separate logical producer payload from rounded retained vector capacity. Shared expression contracts accept actual referenced-column bounds and expose logical result bytes separately from allocation backing. Lock bounds use the actual primary-key columns. INSERT metadata gets a dedicated unit-derived fixed-object envelope, shared by output promises, runtime framing and downstream producer/merge/spool proofs; unrelated raw JSON singleton capacity cannot inflate metadata frames.
decisions.rationale: Native case21 needs59,784,372,035 promised bytes at a3.19GiB RSS and fails22GiB without OOM. Faithful public compilation identifies about25.78GB in two metadata spools and two MergeBlock consumers because raw-row503MB was reused as each metadata-frame limit. Serial key evaluation also counted unreferenced JSON and treated rounded vector stores as logical row payload. These are proof imprecision and resource-policy defects, not grounds to raise the cap or silently disable control.
constraints: Keep current ResultBytes allocation semantics for compatibility; add a distinct logical-result bound. For each affine payload use the smaller of aggregate-input multiplicity and the weighted sum of referenced column bounds. Apply the same bound recursively to expression scratch, Packer, result and encoded keys.
Old callers without per-column information retain conservative behavior. Compiler preserves source lineage and index/type checks; no new independent function whitelist.

A fixed INSERT frame contains BlockInfo/ObjectStats and fixed protocol/header overhead, never raw row contents. Derive maximum object/block metadata from the existing pre-crossing/common-unit flush policy, including partial blocks and a legal wide singleton. Preserve the existing four-copy/fixed-overhead serializer allowance.

Use that same dedicated envelope before runtime serialization and when propagating metadata through MergeBlock, Flush and local spools. Raw join or raw-delete output capacity may remain larger but is not the metadata protocol limit.

Classify modern fixed INSERT only when every MultiUpdateCtx has no DeleteCols. Old Insert.ToWriteS3 is inherently INSERT-only. Preserve the existing conservative raw-delete envelope and semantics; do not apply INSERT bounds to RowID/PK frames or hide unsupported cases as successful imports.

No customer/table names, reduced raw-entry limit, larger memory cap, new tunable threshold, changed SQL/load method or fallback of the failing task. Native acceptance remains three complete39-table rounds under22GiB.

Source descriptors and source-slot envelopes use the same physical makeType/ParallelLoad conversion as External.Prepare. Synthesized hidden filepath values are not raw CSV fields; until a finite static path-size contract exists those graphs select whole-query legacy before Open. Normal customer LOAD graphs remain eligible. Compact CSV column bounds cover inline value bytes through their fixed Varlena headers and must not be confused with header-plus-inline double counting.

JSONLINE parsing and transJson field construction do not yet have a complete conversion scratch/expansion contract. These entire graphs retain legacy before Open; this does not change JSONLINE SQL results and is independent of the successful39-CSV budget repair.

decisions.choice: Forecast null/grouping bitmap growth by examining only the selected source window with Contains, without a prefix iterator.

decisions.choice: Before an ownerless FIFO admission head selects a smaller-than-statically-feasible unit, attempt at most one existing full recovery and reselect from current candidates/physical state.
decisions.rationale: Exact DOP2 public manifest matches native promises: table35 first unit256KiB and10064 local writes/108.34s, second16MiB at DOP1 and66writes/8.68s; table24 units2MiB,4MiB and live1MiB. The current code recovers only when no candidate fits, prematurely preserving reclaimable prior-statement residency by forcing tiny batches.
constraints: Reference the first descending candidate whose full own I+W fits process total; statically impossible targets do not cause performance recovery.
Only candidate API, FIFO head, no tracked tickets/data/IO owner, and not previously reclaimed. Existing active-owner small-fit and legacy single-spec behavior remain unchanged.

Keep the same FIFO node during existing cancellable recovery. On return, recheck cancellation, current physical sample, all input/data/sharedW commitments and any new cross-pool owner. Never reuse the old fit result.
One unsuccessful attempt still grants a currently fitting small candidate; no new sleep/timer/worker/state or DOP-policy change.
This existing full recovery can evict idle arenas/cache(target0), run Go/native reclamation and cold-cache unrelated workloads; record that per-statement cost and measure native throughput.

Retain all failure/cancel/FIFO/unfit paths. Discriminating small-already-fits controls, statically impossible target, activeowner, cancel and crosspool-during-reclaim tests plus exact native continuous import acceptance.

decisions.choice: Separate retry-capable candidate admission from final candidate admission. Add a small optional UntilFit capability on the real throttler, backed by the same existing FIFO/recovery/sample worker. Compiler Parallel>1 retains pressure-driven DOP retry; final Parallel<=1 waits cancellably for dynamic physical pressure to clear and always reselects the largest currently fitting candidate.
decisions.rationale: Native be8 N4 fails an8-row LOAD after28 successes, despite zeroOOM: three5-second-spaced samples show available14,877,761,536 ->16,236,711,936 ->16,853,712,896 versus minimum16,874,101,262. Neighbour samples already exceed minimum within the same retry interval, and exact originalSQL later succeeds in0.284s on the unchanged process without forcedGC/restart. No tracked tickets/data/IO owner is not a proof that whole-process physical residency is irreducible; backend completion can return more arenas after a full recovery.
constraints: Candidate modes immediately reject only min complete I+W greater than known total. Keep existing ordinary single-spec semantics and old provider compatibility.

Reuse one private single/retry/final mode implementation, the same FIFO node, immutable candidate list, owner accounting, physicalFits, one initial full recovery and existing1s coalesced recovery/sample worker. No new waiting timer/worker/queue/threshold, client retry or physical accounting relaxation.
Retain higher-DOP pressure -> real graph recompile; final DOP waiting must not freeze the smallest unit or disable larger-unit reselection when memory later returns.

Cancellation removes the node promptly, stops the last-worker lifecycle, and unblocks successors without waiting for a blocked reclamation callback. Static impossible, invalid sample and late new-owner boundaries remain covered.

Current-statement admission precedes its execution locks, input reader and new I/D/W publication. Frontend transaction/LOCAL pipe and explicit-transaction historical ownership can already exist; cancellation and existing distributed ordered acquisition/rollback remain necessary. Do not claim all process background resources are represented by tracked owners.

Persistent external pressure with a never-cancelled caller cannot simultaneously guarantee finite success and avoid false refusal. Existing caller deadline/cancellation is the termination boundary; no arbitrary internal deadline is introduced.

Full native acceptance must restart a new candidate trial and require at least117 imports plus postchecks; final validation is predeclared as five continuous39-table rounds (195 imports) to observe late-pool and kernel-charge accumulation. N4 remains failed28-success evidence, and the isolated debug success is not a continuous-trial pass.

decisions.choice: For a retry-capable parallel graph, prefer lowering DOP before shrinking the configured target when its largest legal target complete I+W cannot fit even the known empty process limit. Reuse WorkingSetHeadroom.Limit and saturated workingLayoutTotal; unknown or statically fitting targets keep the existing candidate policy. Final graphs still use every candidate with D32 UntilFit.
decisions.rationale: The reviewed N4 source succeeds on its first28 tables but takes297.122s versus243.357s for the same28 baseline tables (+22.09%), excluding later client retry time. Largest table113.317s versus80.4s; DOP2 unit4MiB remains constrained by physical charge even after RSS recovers. Same DOP1 layout supports16MiB with larger remaining physical margin. decisions.choice: Origin transactions marked ByBegin or not explicitly Autocommit use finite immediate bounded admission on every CN. Preserve ordinary autocommit FIFO/UntilFit. Use try-open plus optional NoWait for fail-fast compatibility with previous admission peers.
decisions.rationale: A previous statement can retain transaction workspace or locks until same-session COMMIT/ROLLBACK. Waiting for that memory during LOAD prevents the session reaching COMMIT. Generic recovery cannot free live transaction vectors.
constraints: No admission queue or full-reclaim wait at any DOP; Try all legal candidates once, preserving FIFO fairness, typed capacity, context precedence, DOP retry and reverse partial-CN cleanup.
Keep existing scavenge and short-lock behavior; NoWait does not mean hard realtime or sampling-only. Production recovery callbacks have no identified transaction/pipeline release dependency.

Internal zero-valued txn options conservatively select NoWait; absent transaction test/embedding entrypoints preserve existing behavior. Released non-admission peer/unsupported-graph legacy fallback remains the pre-existing compatibility boundary.

No implicit commit, transaction workspace discard, special data/schema threshold, client retry or shorter timeout. NoWait final pressure can return capacity; no universal finite success claim for irreducible autocommit residency.

decisions.choice: Translate current-process cgroup membership into the selected controller mount coordinates before sampling. Equal root maps to mountpoint; descendants use a component-relative path. Reuse v1 Load/Stat with its selected controller and v2 scalar/stat reader.
decisions.rationale: A private bind exposes an existing cgroup subtree at a new filesystem mountpoint. Concatenating the original hierarchy-absolute membership repeats the subtree and turns valid accounting into a persistent fail-closed wait. The same geometry is valid for v2.
constraints: Read the selected controller directory mount ID with O_PATH and /proc/self/fdinfo, then select that exact mountinfo record. Validate record identity, filesystem/controller, decoded paths and component containment. No guessed first/last/stack order or Kubernetes/memory-size constants.

Validate raw absolute paths before cleaning; reject raw dot/dotdot and noncontained or sibling-prefix geometry as accounting errors, never host fallback. Preserve proven absent-controller versus partial/unreadable accounting classification and retained known limits.

V1 Memory paths always consume the shared validated decoded relative mapping, preserving the same hierarchy/Stat. V2 consumes the localized directory with unchanged readUnifiedMemory. Each O_PATH descriptor closes lexically on all returns; missing/malformed identity remains accounting failure.
Add the existing throttled wait-log accounting error after releasing sample lock. No new metrics labels, endpoint or timer.

Real archived v1 shape plus nearest v1/v2 mappings, escaped paths, wrong aliases/errors, real reader-to-working-ticket consumer, disabled old-path failure and runtime TKE55Gi verification are required. Local v2-only trials cannot establish v1 correctness.

decisions.choice: Rebase the complete thirteen-commit import-memory series onto the exact official v4.1.6-hotfix-20261021 tag and integrate one durable typed-terminal ownership graph. Remove unnecessary ordinary SELECT accounting only where no active output bound consumes it.

pipeline_contract.terminal: Official PipelineEdge is the single authority. Reset publishes durable End/Error independently of Ch2 capacity; Call never sends terminal. Preserve Stop settlement, primary execution/retry errors and cancel siblings before join.
pipeline_contract.retirement: Keep official cache cleanupOnce separate from finalCleanupOnce. Register every real receiver in the existing attempt owner during merge Prepare; all production receiver Init sites are in that shared Prepare. After all local sender/receiver/cleanup joins and remote Stop settlement: release saved current receiver data idempotently on every owned Base; DrainForCleanup every edge (including incoming direct remote frames); final-clean every spool slot; clear registries; detach/release root. Borrowers stay valid until release or proven quiescence.
pipeline_contract.rollback: DiscardUnsent once per unnotified receiver replaces publicationFailed/occupied. No nil-End acknowledgement timeout remains on typed paths.
pipeline_contract.abort_bookkeeping: Construct shardRefs and abortCurrentRefs for all spools before execution; single-receiver no-refcheck fast path depends on receiver count. Include both class-rounded arrays and fixed new fields in MemoryMetadataBound.
pipeline_contract.edge_metadata: Derive final Ch2 capacity conservatively from complete existing producer/scope count and maximum parallel stage, bounded by existing compiler constructor constants. Charge concrete PipelineEdge/durable terminal, old/new Ch2+Done, receiver arrays/reflect select, registry struct and spool/edge/receiver registry append capacity. Count merge receiving edges on their actual CN via existing Receivers descriptor field; local/shared edges may be conservatively counted twice. Validate all future constructor rules and custom channels before Open; unproven/overflow topology stays whole-query legacy.
pipeline_contract.version3: Existing admission capability/manifest version becomes3 because v2 cannot enforce new metadata semantics. New origins require exact3 for every CN before any Open; v0/v2/unknownfuture4 retains whole-query legacy. New server rejects nil/Stage-only/inexact manifests before reserve/reclaim/registration. No new wire field/action. Literal oldv2 origin accepts3>=2 then receives strict rejection/error and reverse-closes already opened tickets; transparent rolling success in that unreleased experimental direction is not promised. Released ed9 peers have no admission capability and preserve ordinary legacy SQL. Token/connection-bound close/abort remains idempotent without manifest.

owned_mpool.terminal_rule: AllocatedBytes decrements after actual Free/deallocation, not before. Same-pool native Realloc updates capacity in one atomic delta. Pool registration removal does not erase a live transferred-buffer counter.

writer.failures: Partial append/write/Sync errors propagate normal errors; temporary quota denial is handled internally without SQL failure or duplicate publication.

workspace.bound: One process budget, bounded bytes and simultaneous permits; IO has reserved capacity that ordinary retained data cannot consume.
workspace.progress: Holder must complete IO/cancel without acquiring normal data grants. No task waiting for a workspace may be the only owner that can release that same workspace.
workspace.minimum: Byte unit is reduced to fit the environment; one irreducible row/minimum working set must fit. Query/import admission must account for source and required operator workspace before normal data fills the available headroom.

broadcast_spill.source: JoinMap owns immutable build FDs and a participant-scoped spill handoff; source closes after final owner. Per-reader logical offsets use ReadAt/SectionReader, never dup+shared Seek.
broadcast_spill.handoff: Each expected probe registers its bounded probe files exactly once, including empty input. The last registrant takes combined work; other probes end. Cancellation aborts coordination and closes unclaimed files.
broadcast_spill.finalize: The consumer runs with one logical finalizer so RIGHT/FULL and directional semi/anti/single matching retain existing semantics.
broadcast_spill.normal_path: No handoff/coordinator is created when the build stays in memory.

skew_fallback.state: Current build chunk only in RAM; probe match sidecar persists across chunk replays; output unmatched probe only after final chunk. Scalar SINGLE detects second match across all chunks using existing SQL error semantics.
skew_fallback.cost: Worst-case IO may be buildChunks times probeBytes; this is an explicit bounded-memory degradation, not a zero-overhead claim.

roles.I: Fixed per-pipeline input/output storage and parser credit, owned until consumption; cannot be borrowed by D/W.
roles.D: Ordinary retained capacity; acquire complete new allocation before mutation; denial causes flush/spill.
roles.W: One process execution slot for destructible spill/encode/IO workspace. Queued jobs hold no slot; no W holder requests D or another W.

working_set_protocol.entry: Compile.prePipelineInitializer before execution locks and InitAllDataSource. Nested execution must inherit a compatible ticket or reserve before parent locks; no hidden recursive admission.
working_set_protocol.topology: Use maximum effective local Scope Mcpu and every independent live input/output stage, including nested/async stages. This is a conservative planning bound; actual broadcast IDs are separately sealed after duplication.
working_set_protocol.I_promise: sum of all live tickets input-slot bytes, including returned output until downstream consumes it
working_set_protocol.W_promise: max(IOBytes of live tickets); exactly one process W job executes
working_set_protocol.atomic: Reserve I increment plus any increase in W maximum atomically before publishing ticket. Reduce target unit and recompute schema envelopes if statically unsatisfiable; a first-admission waiter owns no execution locks or data.
working_set_protocol.unit: min(64 MiB, admissible request unit), reducible before execution. Target is not a new single-row limit.
working_set_protocol.lifetime: Root, active input, queued IO and transferred job hold references. Close cancels queued acquisition and drops root; active jobs remain valid. Final owner removes promises and recomputes W maximum.
working_set_protocol.output: A W job can publish only into a pre-reserved output I slot or transfer an existing D owner without additional blocking allocation. Returned output cannot keep the only W slot while downstream needs W.
working_set_protocol.zero_D: A legal input window borrowed from I can directly spill through W with D full; no clone into D first.
working_set_protocol.physical: U=max(RSS,max(0,cgroupCurrent-inactiveFile)); predicted use adds outstanding I/W/D promises and proposed increase, minus only proven live resident coverage. Default coverage is zero. Raw cgroup current remains observable. This conservatively overcounts resident allocations; performance must be measured.
working_set_protocol.coordination: One process coordinator coalesces sampling/reclaim across throttlers. Denial below RSS soft threshold still requests reclaim. Release wakes immediately. One-second fallback only with waiters. Ordinary FIFO cannot block W.

source_and_writer_revision.capacity: MPool.AllocatedBytes counts current Go and native allocated capacity. Global public offheap stats retain existing meaning. Private pool lives until all transferred buffers free.
source_and_writer_revision.growth: If required exceeds old capacity O, reserve complete new capacity N while O remains charged; never reserve only N-O. Reuse precise vector/mpool growth rules.
source_and_writer_revision.payload: Window byte accounting counts referenced out-of-line varlen payload, inline/null/const semantics and every actual projection; Window.Size is not the bound.
source_and_writer_revision.source_envelope: Q=max(unit,TypedRowUpperBound(configured rawRowLimit,schema)). Include typed old plus complete new capacity, raw record old/new growth, readUntil scratch, unescape/charset temporary storage, fixed parser block and field metadata. SourceEnvelope is calculated from this concrete allocation table.
source_and_writer_revision.raw_limit: Use the existing configured largest-entry-limit support boundary, with no new 64MiB row limit. Inspect parser semantics and prevent complete-record/field-metadata growth bypass before allocation; document compatibility of any corrected bypass.
csv_states: read raw row into parser backing view
before vector mutation compute typed demand and full new capacity
if nonempty batch crosses unit return batch and preserve one pending raw view without reading parser again
singleton above target is allowed within reserved row envelope

Borrowed source I/D is excluded; existing and new scratch coexist in W.
source_and_writer_revision.preextend: PreExtend uses the admitted byte-window row count rather than unconditional 8192 rows.
source_and_writer_revision.writer: Private pool plus manual map/bitmap/capacity ownership is reconciled after mutation. Automatic spill only returns destroyed/transferred capacity; freeList and uncommitted delete stay charged.
source_and_writer_revision.eval: Stream per-writer output instead of out.Append through proc.Mp. Metadata is framed/drained during Build or spooled in bounded frames so a single writer cannot grow unlimited metadata before Eval. Preserve MergeBlock transaction semantics.
source_and_writer_revision.async: Acquire W before executing, transfer with job; queued jobs own input references but no W. Sync may wait for job; job cannot request D/second W. Error/cancel follow same final-owner cleanup.

hashbuild_revision.precopy: Reserve full new vector capacity before copy. Nonblocking denial starts spill with W; no retained-data wait.
hashbuild_revision.prehash: Capacity calculation lives with hashmap allocator and includes load-factor rounding, old+new resize peak, Sels/results/offsets, key-expression/unique-key scratch and iterator/output storage. Use worst row count and checked arithmetic.
hashbuild_revision.denial: Preserve original batches; destroy unpublished partial hashmap; spill original rows; release only destroyed D. Subsequent input spills directly.
hashbuild_revision.publish: Batches, hashmap, Sels and their D leases transfer together to JoinMap and survive until last probe; NeedBatches=false releases only destroyed owners.

broadcast_spill_revision.topology: Each CN probe scope receives stable SpillScopeID; SpillExpectedScopes enumerates its complete per-CN group. Scope duplication seals only its own actual ParallelIDs before Prepare. Composite participant=(scopeID<<32)|parallelID. Build may publish before all scopes seal. Claim requires all expected scopes sealed and all actual participants registered. MessageBoard registry rebuilds the shared local group by JoinMapTag and query epoch across remote scope RPCs.
broadcast_spill_revision.register: Each probe spools bounded private input, including empty stream, releases local W, then registers exactly once. Last participant atomically claims all probe files and immutable build source. Others end without waiting.
broadcast_spill_revision.failure: Registration before-error/IO/cancel/failed Reset aborts epoch. Query-context independent cleanup covers never-started participants. Lock protects ownership transfer only; no IO/allocation/FD-close under coordinator lock.
broadcast_spill_revision.abort: Collecting abort detaches registered files and closes outside lock; unregistered remain local. Claimed abort cancels consumer but never closes its active FD concurrently. Claim/Abort linearize to exactly one terminal owner.
broadcast_spill_revision.bitmap: All probes consult shared spill-generation state, including Reset before JoinMap receive. Spill generation sends/waits on no old bitmapChannel. Claimant executes one logical finalizer; normal in-memory protocol stays unchanged.
broadcast_spill_revision.source: Immutable source and each reader have references. SectionReader/ReadAt gives independent logical offsets; dup plus Seek is forbidden. Source closes only after last source/reader reference.
broadcast_spill_revision.bucket: Every FD explicitly local/queued/active. Pop establishes active ownership before reader creation. Repartition publishes children only after successful completion; all failures close local/active/queued resources exactly once.

spill_codec_revision.compatibility: Original buffer API delegates the common implementation and retains byte-for-byte persistent format. Temporary spill framing uses bounded counting writer and header patching with WriteAt.
spill_codec_revision.framing: No whole-batch serialized copy. Only complete frames are published. Short write, malformed/oversized lengths and encode errors terminate and clean owner.
spill_codec_revision.scatter: All buckets share aggregate byte budget. Flush/shrink before Union or PreExtend. Shared varlen area is compacted into bounded window before serialization; stream API alone is insufficient.

skew_fallback_revision.mode: At max repartition depth, bounded build chunks replay probe files. Never ignore budget and load entire bucket.
skew_fallback_revision.probe_ids: Stable ParticipantID plus local row ordinal survives repartition. Sealed participant prefix yields global probe ID.
skew_fallback_revision.sidecar: Disk-backed match counts/state with bounded page cache, no whole-state RAM bitmap/mmap residency. File bytes/cache/FD count recorded.

remote_execution.entry: Remote decodeScope executes MergeRun without Compile.prePipelineInitializer; admit and attach the local working set and initialize local spill registry before reader/source initialization there, with identical final cleanup.
remote_execution.backward_compatibility: New readers without topology fields keep broadcast builds in memory. Old binaries ignore unknown fields and retain their existing in-memory broadcast path. Every build and all its probe scopes share a CN binary; FDs never cross CN/process/version. Existing shuffle path remains supported.
remote_execution.scope: Narrow extension of pipeline metadata only; no persistent/catalog/SQL protocol format change.

whole_query_admission.manifest: Origin enumerates the complete scope DAG per CN, carrying stage schema/role/retained-field/concurrency descriptors plus statement epoch and incoming frame unit; remote recomputes envelopes using its local configuration. Every scope RPC carries only the token/reference to this same complete local ticket.
whole_query_admission.ordering: Before any execution locks, reads or retained allocation, origin opens/reserves all participating CNs including itself in stable (process UUID,CN UUID) order. Every query uses this order. Partial success is registered for cleanup immediately. DOP recompilation releases every partial ticket before rebuilding.
whole_query_admission.commit: After every CN admits, commit the minimum selected target unit to all CNs. Promise size may shrink, never increase. Receiver input slots still cover the incoming frame bound. Only then execute any pipeline.
whole_query_admission.owner: One dedicated statement admission control stream per remote CN owns the MessageBoard root ticket. Scope RPCs attach/detach references; normal scope cancellation cannot close or abort the shared root. Scope-start and Close are linearized; an absent/closed token is rejected, never recreated.
whole_query_admission.termination: After all remote scopes/notifications join, origin sends END or ABORT with a cleanup context independent of the cancelled query. An acknowledged END permits ordinary stream close. Any failed send/ack/control-context forces Close(true) on the exclusively locked backend, so server SessionCtx.Done runs root cleanup even if END is lost. Server handler defer removes token, closes root and cancels attached unfinished scopes. No forever tombstone or expected-RPC-count cleanup.

Build map stays live while late probe RPC attaches without requesting new I/W
Cancellation before all CNs admit releases partial tickets
END lost or send/ack failure closes independent backend and retires ticket/FDs
Single normal scope cancellation leaves other scopes shared ticket valid
Late attach after root Close is rejected without resurrection

IGNORE and UPDATE publish irregular-index additions only from the final post-dedup projection for both regular-index and pure-irregular-index layouts; only UPDATE deletes old irregular-index entries. REPLACE preserves its existing delete-old behavior.

component_contracts.control_terminal: Control close marks closed/removes token/cancels scopes/closes root WS; shared MessageBoard cleanup waits until all attached scopes detach after operator cleanup. Repeated identical Commit is read-only after publication.
component_contracts.control_transport: Dedicated optional ControlStreamClient uses a separate backend pool, owned/closed by the pipeline client; a control stream cannot occupy the last execution backend. Caller context controls only backend creation/acquisition; returned stream lifetime is independently closed. Existing disconnected server SessionCtx retires on the shared 10s morpc sweep.
component_contracts.expression_key_wire: After eligibility is proved on the full AST, both join-key sides and non-equality predicate are protobuf-marshaled into manifest byte fields; receivers unmarshal without evaluating and derive the same expression capacity. Unknown function allocation contracts and non-NULL varlen literals retain whole-query legacy. Fixed results alone are not a scratch bound; only audited primitive kernels and serial/serial_full are supported.
component_contracts.distributed_unit: All CNs Open before execution, then Commit the global minimum UnitBytes. Therefore each receiver frame is no larger than that receiver own admitted unit (or its already budgeted legal singleton); origin manifests set IncomingUnit=0. Capacity-expression overflow at a large target may shrink unit and retry; malformed descriptors do not.
component_contracts.process_alias: common/runtime.ProcessInstanceID is generated once per process, not per service. GetProtocolVersionResponse optional field3 carries it. Missing process identity retains legacy. Same-process multi-CN is conservatively compatible through legacy; physical manifest merging is outside this fix.

old_insert_revision.eligibility: Only disk ToWriteS3 with an admitted working set uses the new branch. Memory-engine ToWriteS3, partition wrappers, and PreInsert with non-nil CompPkeyExpr or ClusterByExpr retain whole-query legacy before manifest/Open. The latter derived whole-batch expression scratch does not yet have a proven source/input contract; no partial admission or new singleton rejection is introduced. Ordinary Project serial for BTREE is not classified as these PreInsert fields.
old_insert_revision.prepare: Acquire the existing declared output slot, create a private accounted data mpool and separate output mpool, and configure byte unit plus memory workspace on CNS3Writer. Count only InsertCtx.Attrs projection, not hidden input-only columns.
old_insert_revision.append: Cut projected bytes by sum of referenced WindowSize. Reserve complete AppendAllocation before copies; preserve actual owned capacity until destruction. Threshold and cumulative projected retained bytes are at most the actual unit plus one legal crossing singleton. Before crossing, Sync, spool bounded output metadata, and close/recreate buffered writer as required. WithBufferBytes alone does not bound Sync result metadata.
old_insert_revision.denial: Before retry or borrowed IO, retire own destructible buffers via Sync/spool/Close and reconcile to actual allocated bytes. If cold D is still denied, borrow the current input read-only, acquire existing W, WriteBorrowedToFile, release W, and drain bounded results using output I. Never wait for D while retaining I/D/unique W needed for progress.
old_insert_revision.metadata: Take bounded object stats from Sync without expanding them in the D pool. Check metadata vector growth before PreExtend/Expand in output mpool. Preserve original BlockInfo/ObjectStats two-column representation, including different vector lengths. Anonymous length-bounded stream frames live on disk during Build; Eval returns one original-format frame per Call. MergeBlock and transaction protocol remain unchanged.
old_insert_revision.terminal: Error/cancel/Reset/Free join IO and close writer before returning actual D; clean output vectors before output lease release; close anonymous spool exactly once. Partial initialization schedules cleanup immediately. Reset starts an independent generation with no stale output frame.
old_insert_revision.flush_limiter: Legacy limiter waits only while active slot owners exist. Their release closes notify, and context cancellation independently terminates. Remove the 200ms timer and20ms ticker; a CPU concurrency-limit increase is observed at the next guaranteed active-owner release.

states.retired: Terminal once; Reset-to-Free and duplicate cleanup perform no new group transition.

compiler_hooks.pkg/sql/compile/scope.go:newParallelScop: Seal template only. Arm Mcpu1 original as actual; for Mcpu>1 arm actual roots after construction and PreScopes publication, never the unused template.

compiler_hooks.pkg/sql/compile/scope.go:cleanPipelineWi: Arm instantiated Normal actual before failed cleanup when scheduler submit fails before Prepare.

broadcast_participant_revision9.epoch: Ownership is bound to the actual generation. Stale template/retired handles never affect a later epoch; rearm only at next actual execution/Prepare.
broadcast_participant_revision9.owner: Existing group owns transferred files; existing work owner closes active readers/files. No new cross-CN FD transfer or registry.
broadcast_participant_revision9.compatibility: No protobuf, persistent format, SQL or memory-envelope change. Legacy non-spill execution keeps its existing protocol.
broadcast_participant_revision9.normal_completion: Expected/registered cleanup is classified with pipelineFailed/explicit err plus operator execution-complete state. Normal non-spilled or empty-build completion calls FinishParticipant once; it must not abort. Premature expected termination, error or spilled incomplete collection aborts the owning generation.

problem.reachability: Frontend permits LOAD in an active transaction; prior INSERT/DELETE workspace and locks can survive EndStatement/IncrStatementID. This is source-proven conditional reachability, not an assertion that N5 encountered it.
cycle: LOAD waits for memory/owner release at admission, including final ownerless UntilFit or active-owner FIFO waiting
Some decisive residency or lock/workspace belongs to the same explicit/non-autocommit transaction, strongly referenced by prior statements
Ordinary release requires same session to COMMIT/ROLLBACK, or a safe transaction-owned spill absent from generic recovery
Sequential session reaches COMMIT/ROLLBACK only after LOAD returns
problem.pressure_witness: Let M=min candidate I+W, B=irreducible nontransaction residency, H=live prior-transaction residency, L=physical limit. B+M<=L<B+H+M and M<=L gives static feasible but dynamic no progress if no external release/cancel occurs.

invariants: An already eligible bounded import whose origin transaction is ByBegin OR !Autocommit must not enqueue/wait on resource-admission FIFO at any DOP, irrespective of recognized owners. It still reserves a complete bounded working ticket if immediately possible.

Origin owns transaction policy. The same optional NoWait manifest bit is copied to every local and remote CN manifest before any open. A remote operator must not rederive policy from snapshot/default txn options.

NoWait tries every finite legal descending candidate at most once with the existing TryReserveWorkingSet. It never calls ReserveWorkingSet, ReserveCandidates, UntilFit, ReclaimForWorkingSet, or installs a worker/waiter. Each successful try atomically respects the existing FIFO and physical commitments.

Normal known autocommit (ByBegin=false,Autocommit=true) and nil-origin-txn embedding fixtures follow exactly the existing D32/D33 admission paths. No implicit commit, workspace discard, forced rollback, plan special case, threshold, client retry, short deadline, or legacy fallback is introduced to avoid pressure.

A failed higher-DOP NoWait request preserves the existing CapacityError-to-DOP-recompile path. A failed final-DOP NoWait request returns the existing typed WorkingSetCapacityError with zero newly installed ImportMemory or leaked CN tickets.

existing_refresh_audit.definition: NoWait means no admission FIFO wait, no full-reclaim wait, no waiting for another ticket/transaction to free memory. It does not promise hard realtime, no mutex acquisition, or zero GC/native scavenging latency.
existing_refresh_audit.not_read_only: TryReserveWorkingSet calls Refresh; WorkingSetHeadroom force-refreshes. Both refresh paths can run existing best-effort RSS scavenging. Never describe them as sampling-only.
edges: Try validates spec and context; Refresh takes m.refreshMu, samples under c.sampleMu, releases sampleMu, updates atomics; actual readProcessMemory reads /proc/cgroup plus total-memory metadata only.

Existing tryScavengeRSS may take rssScavengeMu and call CN cache target setter/clearer. Those production callbacks take only fileservice memCachePressureMu, update owner map/atomic target/deadline, and call no cache eviction/txn/admission method while holding it.

Actual cache eviction callback runs asynchronously in a separate goroutine with existing bounded eviction context; it is not joined by Try. c.cacheMu is released before that goroutine calls c.releaseGo, so no cacheMu->goMu held edge.

Synchronous c.releaseGo takes goMu and calls debug.FreeOSMemory; synchronous c.releaseNative takes nativeMu and calls malloc.ReleaseUnusedMemory -> libc malloc_trim(0). Neither production callback waits for txn commit, a pipeline channel, admission ticket, or c.mu. Live txn vectors remain referenced; GC cannot free them. Ordinary runtime/libc internal locks are finite implementation synchronization, not a resource-release protocol.

Full reclaim may separately hold reclaimMu and then use cache/go/native locks, but releases those locks before m.refresh(true). c.run similarly finishes each callback/lock before refresh. Thus an existing concurrent full reclaim can add ordinary mutex latency, but no found reverse refreshMu<->goMu/nativeMu/cacheMu lock edge holds across refresh; NoWait itself never invokes or joins fullDone.
After Refresh, Try takes c.mu, rechecks context and current FIFO/physical commitments, grants atomically or immediately denies. It never holds c.mu while sampling/scavenging or waiting for a ticket.

common_mapping_contract.inputs: Raw decoded mountinfo root R and mountpoint M, raw process membership P from the same process namespace. Metadata I/O is an ordinary sample operation, not a new hot row path. No global mutable injection or cache.

Open M with unix.O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC and immediately defer unix.Close in the same function. Read /proc/self/fdinfo/<ownedfd> and parse exactly one positive decimal mnt_id. While FD remains owned, match exactly one mountinfo record with that ID and verify its decoded mountpoint==M, fs type (v1 cgroup/v2 cgroup2), and v1 exact memory super-option token. Missing/invalid/duplicate fdinfo key or selected mountinfo ID, permission/read error and identity/type/token mismatch are ordinary accounting errors, never root or host fallback.
common_mapping_contract.format: Parse mountinfo using its " - " separator (not a fixed count of optional fields); decode standard \040/\011/\012/\134 path escapes. Require clean absolute raw P/R/M and reject raw dot/dotdot components BEFORE any filepath.Clean/Join can erase them.
common_mapping_contract.mapping: Compute filepath.Rel(R,P) only after raw validation. Equality yields local "/"; descendants yield "/"+relative; reject rel==".." or a component-prefixed "../". Component checks reject /tenant/container2 as a descendant of /tenant/container. Resolve under M only after validation.
common_mapping_contract.no_fallback: A mapping error is an ordinary accounting error, not errNoMemoryController. Do not fall back to M itself, old M+P, host memory, a directory selected by file existence, or a customer/runtime-specific prefix.
